roadmap.lecture_goal: understand the theoretical framework and practical algorithms used to optimize VR pathfinding for enhanced user experience.

objectives.text: You'll be able to compare path optimization methods by introducing the time threshold constraint, formulate the importance of nodes and paths, and calculate total waiting time for a path.
You'll be able to define the VR path optimization problem using the Vehicle Routing Problem with Profit (VRPP) and outline the multi-stage algorithm for optimizing VR pathfinding with wait times.
You'll be able to summarize the advanced pathfinding methods for optimizing VR experience and mitigating cyber sickness.

segments.subgoal: Compare path optimization methods by introducing the time threshold constraint

key_points.text: The new approach seeks to find an optimal path that covers the maximum number of points of interest (POIs) given a specific time constraint (8, 12).
A time threshold (TTH) is defined to restrict the user's movement time and prevent the possibility of cyber sickness (19, 20, 22).
The time threshold can be determined through empirical studies with users or by using pre-existing study results (30, 32).
Unlike the previous method, the new approach does not require the user to visit every single node or point of interest (33, 34).

segments.subgoal: Define the VR path optimization problem using the Vehicle Routing Problem with Profit (VRPP)

key_points.text: The revised problem aims to maximize total importance (FP) for paths that complete within a specific time threshold (T threshold).
This problem is identified as a generalization of the Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP), known as VRP with Profit (VRPP).
The core objective is to maximize profit (importance) within the given time constraint without requiring the visit of all nodes.
Existing VRPP solvers can be utilized to find the optimal path that maximizes profit within the time constraint.

segments.subgoal: Outline the multi-stage algorithm for optimizing VR pathfinding with wait times

key_points.text: The goal is to find an optimal path (P) that maximizes importance (F) while keeping the total exposure time (travel time plus wait time) below a specified threshold.
The initial graph must be converted into a complete graph (G dash) by replacing non-connected edges with shortest paths.
Edge weights in the modified graph are replaced with travel time, which is computed using the natural walking model.
The VRPP solver is used on the final graph (G double dash), providing importance (F) and waiting time (W) as inputs to determine the optimal path (P opt).
The final optimal path must be modified to reflect the original graph by replacing hypothetical shortest-path edges.

segments.subgoal: Summarize the advanced pathfinding methods for optimizing VR experience and mitigating cyber sickness

key_points.text: The initial approach of finding a minimum time path may not address cyber sickness concerns if the time is still large.

The goal of the optimal path is to cover the maximum number of most important POIs within a given time threshold.
The next part of the lecture will apply these optimization ideas to the course case study.

How do the objectives and constraints of these two approaches differ, and in what scenario would each be most appropriate?
